answers.question: Is crime rising or falling in Bernal Heights, San Francisco (past year vs the year before, as of mid-2026)?
answers.answer:
Crime in Bernal Heights has generally *fallen* over the past year (mid-2025 through mid-2026 compared to the year before). Public Analyst.ai data shows significant drops in several key categories: burglary down ~45%, theft from vehicles down ~55%, other larceny down ~60%, motor vehicle theft ~47%, and robbery ~30%. ([publicanalyst.ai](https://www.publicanalyst.ai/neighborhood/san-francisco/bernal-heights?utm_source=openai))

There is one outlier: arson has shown a modest increase (~11%) over that same period. But overall, the trend is a strong decrease in both violent and property crime in Bernal Heights. ([publicanalyst.ai](https://www.publicanalyst.ai/neighborhood/san-francisco/bernal-heights?utm_source=openai))

answers.question: Is crime rising or falling in Japantown, San Francisco (past year vs the year before, as of mid-2026)?
answers.answer:
Crime in Japantown appears to be falling over the past year compared to the prior period (mid-2025 vs mid-2024). According to Safemap, incident rates in Japantown have declined by about 56% over the analyzed period, with an average of ~5 incidents/month and a distinct downward trend. ([safemap.io](https://safemap.io/sf/reports/neighborhood/japantown?utm_source=openai))

City-wide, San Francisco also saw significant drops in crime: total incidents are down ~7.2%, property crime down ~25%, and violent crime down ~8–9% year-to-date through late May 2026 vs the same period in 2025. ([transparent.city](https://transparent.city/c/san-francisco/stories/hZWfqkxN?utm_source=openai))

answers.question: Is crime rising or falling in Outer Mission, San Francisco (past year vs the year before, as of mid-2026)?
answers.answer:

answers.question: I'm considering moving to the Tenderloin in San Francisco. Is crime there getting better or worse as of mid-2026?
answers.answer:
As of mid-2026, crime in the Tenderloin is a mixed picture — improving in many categories, but worsening in others.  

**Highlights of improvement:**
- Robberies have trended downward: the neighborhood saw a ~13% year-over-year drop in monthly robbery counts as of June 2026. ([publicanalyst.ai](https://www.publicanalyst.ai/neighborhood/san-francisco/tenderloin?utm_source=openai))  
- Overall violent and property crime citywide — including in the Tenderloin — have declined in the first half of 2026. ([sfchronicle.com](https://www.sfchronicle.com/crime/article/san-francisco-homicide-data-22322670.php?utm_source=openai))  
- Homicides in the Tenderloin remain very low: only 1 recorded so far in 2026, compared to higher numbers in prior years. ([media.api.sf.gov](https://media.api.sf.gov/documents/PoliceCommission12126_-_Commission_Crime_Trends.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

**Areas that are getting worse:**
- Drug‐offense incidents in the Tenderloin are rising sharply: through mid‐May 2026 they're up about 70% from the same period in 2025, and the Tenderloin is now the top neighborhood for drug incidents in the city. ([transparent.city](https://transparent.city/c/san-francisco/stories/GNZ9DU6r?utm_source=openai))  
- Assaults (non-violent and misdemeanor-level) have increased in some reports, though trends vary by crime type. ([sanfranciscopolice.org](https://www.sanfranciscopolice.org/sites/default/files/2026-04/SFPD_CrimeReport_Feb2026_20260402.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

**Bottom line:**  
Crime in the Tenderloin is generally *getting better* when it comes to property crimes, homicides, and robberies, but *getting worse* with respect to drug offenses and certain assault categories. If you move there, expect improvements still, but also ongoing challenges, particularly around drugs.

answers.question: 311 noise complaints in San Francisco rose over 60% in the year to mid-2026. Does that mean the city actually got dramatically louder?
answers.answer:
A 60%+ jump in 311 noise complaints is alarming, but it doesn’t automatically mean the city is dramatically louder. Multiple factors can drive more complaints without a proportionate increase in noise:

- Reporting behavior might have changed: people may be more sensitive to noise, more aware of 311, or more willing to file complaints.  
- A few recurring sources—like weekly protests at a particular intersection—can skew totals. For example, a protest at Van Ness & O’Farrell generated large spikes in complaints tied to that event. ([sfchronicle.com](https://www.sfchronicle.com/sf/article/protest-noise-complaints-22325742.php?utm_source=openai))  
- The increase covers all noise types—from traffic to construction to dogs—which may not have gotten uniformly louder. ([311info.com](https://311info.com/city/san_francisco/noise/?utm_source=openai))  

If you want, I can try looking up decibel-level measurements over time in different parts of SF to see if they confirm an actual increase in ambient noise.
